## Hardening / quality
- **A. Undo/Redo via `NSUndoManager`** — wire the context's undo manager to the window, so create/edit/delete and group changes are all undoable. Big "real Mac app" win, modest effort, builds directly on `ContactStore`. Fully testable. *(My pick — see bottom.)*
- **B. Accessibility pass** — audit every interactive control for VoiceOver labels/hints/values, full keyboard navigation, Dynamic Type support. I can do the code work; you'd verify with VoiceOver.
- **C. UI tests via XCUITest** — adds a new test target for real click-through journeys (open app → create contact → enter fields → find duplicates → merge). Slower than unit tests, but extends the safety net to the UI layer.
- **D. Swift 6 strict concurrency** — bump `SWIFT_VERSION` to 6 and clean up the resulting data-race warnings. Future-proofs the codebase. Real risk of churn; useful but not urgent.

## Core features
- **E. macOS **Contacts framework** bridge** — import/export with the system Contacts.app (the canonical Mac contact store). Unlocks Mail/Messages interop. Needs Contacts permission entitlement.
- **F. App Intents + Spotlight indexing** — index contacts in Spotlight; expose "Create Contact" / "Find Contact" / "Open Group" as Shortcuts and Siri intents. Modern Mac integration with a small API surface.
- **G. Drag-and-drop** — drag a contact or selection to Finder to write a `.vcf`, drop a `.vcf` onto the list to import, drop an image onto the avatar. Standard mac behavior; very testable manually.
- **H. Preferences scene** — `Settings { ... }` with default sort, default-group-for-new-contacts, "hide empty fields in detail," and a Restore Defaults. Small but useful.

## Polish & UX
- **I. Multi-window** — `OpenWindowAction` + `WindowGroup(for: PersistentIdentifier.self)` so a contact can open in its own window. Tahoe-native pattern.
- **J. MapKit embed in the inspector** for the contact's address — small, visual, fully verifiable.

## Migration / interop
- **K. CSV import** — frequent migration path from Google/Outlook exports.
- **L. iOS/iPad target sharing the SwiftData schema + ContactStore** — biggest jump in surface, opens the door to iPhone sync via the CloudKit container you'll wire up.

---

## My top pick
**Start with A — Undo/Redo.**

Why: it's a core Mac affordance users will reach for and miss; it lands almost free given our architecture (every `ContactStore` mutation is already atomic), it doesn't need an entitlement or a device, and the journey tests against `ContactStore` make it easy to verify *behavior* (undo a create → store empty; undo a merge → both contacts back). With the inspector and the CloudKit-ready container in place, undo is the missing piece that makes this feel like a real Mac app.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/ContactLink.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactLink.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Builds the `mailto:` / `tel:` URLs behind the contact detail's\n//  click-to-mail and click-to-call actions. Kept here (not in the view) so\n//  the value normalization — which is the part that actually has edge cases\n//  — is unit-tested directly.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum ContactLink {\n    /// A `mailto:` URL for an email address, or `nil` if it's blank.\n    /// The address is percent-encoded so an odd value can't produce a\n    /// malformed URL (`@` and `+` are left intact — both are legal here).\n    static func mailto(_ email: String) -> URL? {\n        let trimmed = email.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        guard !trimmed.isEmpty,\n              let encoded = trimmed.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed)\n        else { return nil }\n        return URL(string: \"mailto:\\(encoded)\")\n    }\n\n    /// A `tel:` URL for a phone number, or `nil` if it carries no digits.\n    /// Keeps only the dialable digits plus a leading `+` (country code),\n    /// dropping the spaces, parentheses, and dashes people type for\n    /// readability — matching how `ContactStore` normalizes phone values.\n    static func tel(_ phone: String) -> URL? {\n        let trimmed = phone.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        let digits = String(trimmed.filter(\\.isNumber))\n        guard !digits.isEmpty else { return nil }\n        let prefix = trimmed.hasPrefix(\"+\") ? \"+\" : \"\"\n        return URL(string: \"tel:\\(prefix)\\(digits)\")\n    }\n}\n"
}

Three comments — two valid, one incorrect. My assessment:

1. **`actionURL` "won't compile"** — incorrect. It's a Swift 5.9 `switch` expression with implicit return (the same form used elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. `ContactStoreError.errorDescription`). It built fine — `make check` is green and CI passed. I'll push back with that.

3. **tel doc comment inaccurate** — valid. `ContactStore.normalizedValue` strips the `+` too; my comment implies full parity. I'll correct the wording.

> AGENT

No versioned migration plan exists, and the container is CloudKit-backed — and **you can't change a field's type in a deployed CloudKit schema** (changes must be additive). So migrating `Date? → DateComponents?` is off the table for a focused fix. The correct, migration-safe, CloudKit-safe fix is to keep `Date?` but anchor birthdays to a **fixed UTC calendar** everywhere (storage interpretation, vCard, Contacts, and the DatePicker), so the calendar day is timezone-invariant — plus parse the vCard no-year `--MMDD` form so it's no longer dropped.   "content": "//\n//  Birthday.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  A birthday is a date-only value, but the model persists it as `Date`\n//  (retyping the stored attribute would break the CloudKit schema, whose\n//  fields can only be added, not changed). To keep \"the day\" unambiguous\n//  regardless of the device's time zone — and across CloudKit sync between\n//  devices in different zones — every birthday `Date` is anchored to UTC and\n//  always read back through the same calendar here. Without this, a `Date`\n//  set at local midnight in one zone reads as the previous/next day in\n//  another (the Tokyo→US day-shift).\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum Birthday {\n    /// Gregorian calendar pinned to UTC — the single source of truth for\n    /// turning a birthday into and out of a `Date`. Used by `VCard`,\n    /// `ContactsBridge`, and the detail-view `DatePicker` so all three agree\n    /// on which calendar day a stored `Date` represents.\n    static let calendar: Calendar = {\n        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)\n        calendar.timeZone = .gmt\n        return calendar\n    }()\n\n    /// Year stored for birthdays whose source omitted it (a vCard `--MMDD`,\n    /// or a Contacts card with no year). Predates any living person, so export\n    /// can recognize it and round-trip back to the year-less form rather than\n    /// emitting a fabricated year.\n    static let omittedYear = 1604\n\n    /// Builds a UTC-anchored birthday `Date` from calendar fields. A `nil`\n    /// `year` means \"year unknown\" and stores the sentinel.\n    static func date(year: Int?, month: Int, day: Int) -> Date? {\n        var components = DateComponents()\n        components.year = year ?? omittedYear\n        components.month = month\n        components.day = day\n        return calendar.date(from: components)\n    }\n\n    /// Splits a birthday `Date` back into UTC calendar fields, reporting\n    /// `year == nil` when it carries the omitted-year sentinel.\n    static func fields(of date: Date) -> (year: Int?, month: Int, day: Int) {\n        let parts = calendar.dateComponents([.year, .month, .day], from: date)\n        let year = parts.year == omittedYear ? nil : parts.year\n        return (year, parts.month ?? 1, parts.day ?? 1)\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "    /// Serializes a birthday to a vCard `BDAY` value. A known year uses the\n    /// ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` form; an unknown year (the `Birthday` sentinel) uses\n    /// the year-less `--MMDD` form so it survives a round-trip.\n    private static func bday(from birthday: Date) -> String {\n        let fields = Birthday.fields(of: birthday)\n        if let year = fields.year {\n            return String(format: \"%04d-%02d-%02d\", year, fields.month, fields.day)\n        }\n        return String(format: \"--%02d%02d\", fields.month, fields.day)\n    }\n\n    /// Parses a vCard `BDAY` value into a UTC-anchored birthday `Date`.\n    /// Accepts the year-less `--MMDD` / `--MM-DD` forms (returning a sentinel\n    /// year) as well as `YYYY-MM-DD` / `YYYYMMDD`, ignoring any time suffix.\n    /// Returns `nil` when no month/day can be read, so a junk value is dropped\n    /// rather than mis-parsed.\n    private static func parseBirthday(_ value: String) -> Date? {\n        let trimmed = value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        if trimmed.hasPrefix(\"--\") {\n            let digits = trimmed.dropFirst(2).filter(\\.isNumber)\n            guard digits.count >= 4,\n                  let month = Int(digits.prefix(2)),\n                  let day = Int(digits.dropFirst(2).prefix(2))\n            else { return nil }\n            return Birthday.date(year: nil, month: month, day: day)\n        }\n        let datePart = trimmed.split(separator: \"T\").first.map(String.init) ?? trimmed\n        let digits = datePart.filter(\\.isNumber)\n        guard digits.count >= 8,\n              let year = Int(digits.prefix(4)),\n              let month = Int(digits.dropFirst(4).prefix(2)),\n              let day = Int(digits.dropFirst(6).prefix(2))\n        else { return nil }\n        return Birthday.date(year: year, month: month, day: day)\n    }"
}

(One-time caveat:\na birthday created under the old local-midnight convention in a zone east\nof UTC may shift back a day on first read; new edits are stable.)\n\nTests: VCard round-trips a yeared and a year-less birthday and parses the\nextended `--MM-DD`; ContactsBridge maps a yeared and a year-less card.\nExisting birthday assertions now read through the UTC calendar so they're\nmachine-time-zone-independent. 115 unit tests + 3 UI tests green.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"\ngit push -u origin fix/birthday-timezone 2>&1 | tail -3",

> AGENT

Three substantive comments. My assessment:

1. **Sentinel 1604 collides with a real 1604 birthday** — valid (the app's own samples are historical figures, so a 1604 birth year isn't far-fetched). I'll move the sentinel to a **future leap year** (impossible for a real *past* birthday; leap so Feb 29 no-year birthdays survive) and add a regression test that 1604 keeps its year.
2. **CSV import still uses `.autoupdatingCurrent` + only `yyyy-MM-dd`** — valid and important; I missed that path. My "everywhere" claim was wrong. I'll route CSV through the same `Birthday` parsing.
3. **DatePicker shows the sentinel year for no-year birthdays** — valid UX point, but a month/day-only picker is a separate, larger UI change; no-year birthdays only arrive via import. I'll reply with the rationale and spin off a follow-up.

  "new_string": "    /// Splits a birthday `Date` back into UTC calendar fields, reporting\n    /// `year == nil` when it carries the omitted-year sentinel.\n    static func fields(of date: Date) -> Fields {\n        let parts = calendar.dateComponents([.year, .month, .day], from: date)\n        let year = parts.year == omittedYear ? nil : parts.year\n        return Fields(year: year, month: parts.month ?? 1, day: parts.day ?? 1)\n    }\n\n    /// Parses a date-only birthday string into a UTC-anchored `Date`. Accepts\n    /// the year-less `--MMDD` / `--MM-DD` forms (storing the sentinel year) as\n    /// well as `YYYY-MM-DD` / `YYYYMMDD`, ignoring any `T` time suffix.\n    /// Returns `nil` when no month/day can be read, so junk is dropped rather\n    /// than mis-parsed. Shared by the vCard and CSV importers so every entry\n    /// path lands on the same UTC convention.\n    static func parse(_ string: String) -> Date? {\n        let trimmed = string.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        if trimmed.hasPrefix(\"--\") {\n            let digits = trimmed.dropFirst(2).filter(\\.isNumber)\n            guard digits.count >= 4,\n                  let month = Int(digits.prefix(2)),\n                  let day = Int(digits.dropFirst(2).prefix(2))\n            else { return nil }\n            return date(year: nil, month: month, day: day)\n        }\n        let datePart = trimmed.split(separator: \"T\").first.map(String.init) ?? trimmed\n        let digits = datePart.filter(\\.isNumber)\n        guard digits.count >= 8,\n              let year = Int(digits.prefix(4)),\n              let month = Int(digits.dropFirst(4).prefix(2)),\n              let day = Int(digits.dropFirst(6).prefix(2))\n        else { return nil }\n        return date(year: year, month: month, day: day)\n    }\n}"

1	//
2	//  VCardTransfer.swift
3	//  ContactManager
4	//
5	//  A `Transferable` wrapping a single contact's vCard payload + suggested
6	//  filename. Dragging a row hands one of these to Finder, which receives
7	//  a `.vcf` file named after the contact.
8	//
9	
10	import Foundation
11	import SwiftUI
12	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
13	
14	struct VCardTransfer: Transferable {
15	    /// File-system-safe stem, without the `.vcf` extension. Computed by
16	    /// `suggestedFilename(for:)` so the sanitization is testable.
17	    let suggestedName: String
18	    /// The vCard 3.0 text the file will contain.
19	    let text: String
20	
21	    static var transferRepresentation: some TransferRepresentation {
22	        FileRepresentation(exportedContentType: .vCard) { transfer in
23	            // Write to a per-drag tempdir so multiple drags don't collide on
24	            // a shared filename. Finder copies the file out by the time the
25	            // OS clears the temp dir at next launch.
26	            let directory = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
27	                .appending(path: "vcard-drag-\(UUID().uuidString)")
28	            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
29	                at: directory, withIntermediateDirectories: true
30	            )
31	            let url = directory.appending(path: "\(transfer.suggestedName).vcf")
32	            try Data(transfer.text.utf8).write(to: url)
33	            return SentTransferredFile(url, allowAccessingOriginalFile: false)
34	        }
35	    }
36	
37	    /// Pure helper: produces a filename stem ("Ada Lovelace") from the
38	    /// contact's `fullName`, falling back to "Contact" for an unnamed one
39	    /// and stripping characters that are illegal on macOS file systems.
40	    static func suggestedFilename(for displayName: String) -> String {
41	        let trimmed = displayName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
42	        let base = trimmed.isEmpty ? "Contact" : trimmed
43	        // Forward slash and colon are the only path-illegal characters on
44	        // HFS+/APFS; replace them rather than dropping them so two distinct
45	        // names don't collapse into one.
46	        return base
47	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "/", with: "-")
48	            .replacingOccurrences(of: ":", with: "-")
49	    }
50	}
51

292	    private func handleImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {
293	        switch result {
294	        case .failure(let error):
295	            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
296	        case .success(let url):
297	            Task {
298	                // Read the file and run the avatar pipeline off the main actor
299	                // so a multi-megabyte photo can't hitch the UI.
300	                let avatar: Data? = await Task.detached {
301	                    let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
302	                    defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }
303	                    // Decode straight from the file via ImageIO so a huge image
304	                    // is downsampled to a thumbnail without ever loading its

ID 3368473141 — ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView.swift:97
`onNameFieldFocused()` is invoked immediately after setting `nameFieldFocused = true`. If SwiftUI hasn't actually applied focus yet (timing/layout), the parent flag will be cleared and the view won't retry, leaving the cursor unfocused. Clear the flag only after the field is confirmed focused (e.g., via `onChange` of the `@FocusState`).
---
ID 3368473149 — ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView+Photo.swift:13
These photo action handlers mutate `@State` (`errorMessage`) and call into `ContactStore`/SwiftData. Marking them `@MainActor` makes the UI mutation and model context usage actor-safe regardless of which thread/actor the importer/drop callback happens to run on.
---
ID 3368473153 — ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView+Photo.swift:44
`removePhoto()` updates SwiftData via `store` and mutates `errorMessage`; it should be main-actor isolated like the rest of the UI-facing mutations.
---
```

> AGENT

Three valid comments. My take:
1. **Clear the flag only after focus lands** — right; clearing immediately risks a no-retry miss. I'll clear via `onChange` of the `@FocusState`.
2 & 3. **`@MainActor` on the photo handlers** — they mutate `@State` and use the SwiftData context; explicit main-actor isolation is correct.

Let me apply all three.

  "old_string": "        // A freshly created contact opens with the cursor in First Name so you\n        // can type a name immediately instead of reaching for the mouse.\n        .onAppear {\n            if focusNameField {\n                nameFieldFocused = true\n                onNameFieldFocused()\n            }\n        }",

}

//
//  VCardTransferTests.swift
//  ContactManagerTests
//
//  Filename sanitization for the drag-to-Finder export.
//

@testable import ContactManager
import Testing

struct VCardTransferTests {
    @Test func usesContactNameWhenPresent() {
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "Ada Lovelace") == "Ada Lovelace")
    }

    @Test func fallsBackToContactForEmptyName() {
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "") == "Contact")
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "   ") == "Contact")
    }

    @Test func replacesPathIllegalCharacters() {
        // `/` and `:` are illegal in HFS+/APFS filenames; both should be
        // rewritten rather than dropped so two distinct names don't collide.
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "AC/DC") == "AC-DC")
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "9:30 Club") == "9-30 Club")
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "/:/") == "---")
    }

    @Test func keepsInternationalCharacters() {
        #expect(VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: "Søren Kierkegaard") == "Søren Kierkegaard")
    }
}

{
  "replace_all": false,

  "old_string": "struct VCardTransfer: Transferable {\n    /// File-system-safe stem, without the `.vcf` extension. Computed by\n    /// `suggestedFilename(for:)` so the sanitization is testable.\n    let suggestedName: String\n    /// The vCard 3.0 text the file will contain.\n    let text: String\n\n    static var transferRepresentation: some TransferRepresentation {\n        FileRepresentation(exportedContentType: .vCard) { transfer in\n            // Write to a per-drag tempdir so multiple drags don't collide on\n            // a shared filename. Finder copies the file out by the time the\n            // OS clears the temp dir at next launch.\n            let directory = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory\n                .appending(path: \"vcard-drag-\\(UUID().uuidString)\")\n            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(\n                at: directory, withIntermediateDirectories: true\n            )\n            let url = directory.appending(path: \"\\(transfer.suggestedName).vcf\")\n            try Data(transfer.text.utf8).write(to: url)\n            return SentTransferredFile(url, allowAccessingOriginalFile: false)\n        }\n    }",
  "new_string": "struct VCardTransfer: Transferable {\n    /// Encoded `PersistentIdentifier` of the source contact, so an in-app drop\n    /// (e.g. onto a sidebar group) can resolve which contact was dragged. Empty\n    /// when the identity isn't relevant (e.g. the detail Share button).\n    var contactID: String = \"\"\n    /// File-system-safe stem, without the `.vcf` extension. Computed by\n    /// `suggestedFilename(for:)` so the sanitization is testable.\n    let suggestedName: String\n    /// The vCard 3.0 text the file will contain.\n    let text: String\n\n    static var transferRepresentation: some TransferRepresentation {\n        // Dragging to Finder (or another app) writes a `.vcf` file.\n        FileRepresentation(exportedContentType: .vCard) { transfer in\n            // Write to a per-drag tempdir so multiple drags don't collide on\n            // a shared filename. Finder copies the file out by the time the\n            // OS clears the temp dir at next launch.\n            let directory = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory\n                .appending(path: \"vcard-drag-\\(UUID().uuidString)\")\n            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(\n                at: directory, withIntermediateDirectories: true\n            )\n            let url = directory.appending(path: \"\\(transfer.suggestedName).vcf\")\n            try Data(transfer.text.utf8).write(to: url)\n            return SentTransferredFile(url, allowAccessingOriginalFile: false)\n        }\n        // Dropping within the app exposes just the contact id as plain text, so\n        // a sidebar group can add the dragged contact without parsing a vCard.\n        ProxyRepresentation(exporting: \\.contactID)\n    }"
}

{

  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/ContactStore.swift",
  "old_string": "    // MARK: - Merge duplicates",
  "new_string": "    /// Adds the contacts named by their encoded `PersistentIdentifier`s to\n    /// `group` — the data path behind dragging contacts onto a sidebar group.\n    /// Ids that don't resolve and contacts already in the group are skipped;\n    /// returns how many were actually added (0 means no save/undo step).\n    @discardableResult\n    func addContacts(withEncodedIDs ids: [String], to group: ContactGroup) throws -> Int {\n        let wanted = Set(ids)\n        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return 0 }\n        let groupID = group.persistentModelID\n        let toAdd = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<Contact>()).filter { contact in\n            wanted.contains(contact.persistentModelID.storedString ?? \"\")\n                && !contact.groups.contains { $0.persistentModelID == groupID }\n        }\n        guard !toAdd.isEmpty else { return 0 }\n        return try mutate(\"Add to Group\") {\n            toAdd.forEach { $0.groups.append(group) }\n            return toAdd.count\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Merge duplicates"
}

  "content": "//\n//  GroupDropTests.swift\n//  ContactManagerTests\n//\n//  Covers `ContactStore.addContacts(withEncodedIDs:to:)` — the data path\n//  behind dragging contacts from the list onto a sidebar group.\n//\n\n@testable import ContactManager\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\nimport Testing\n\n@MainActor\n@Suite(.serialized)\nstruct GroupDropTests {\n    let container: ModelContainer\n    let store: ContactStore\n\n    init() throws {\n        container = try ModelContainer(\n            for: Contact.self, ContactField.self, ContactGroup.self,\n            configurations: ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: true)\n        )\n        store = ContactStore(container.mainContext)\n    }\n\n    @Test func addsDroppedContactsToTheGroup() throws {\n        let group = try store.createGroup(named: \"Work\")\n        let ada = try store.createContact()\n        let alan = try store.createContact()\n        let ids = try [ada, alan].map { try #require($0.persistentModelID.storedString) }\n\n        let added = try store.addContacts(withEncodedIDs: ids, to: group)\n        #expect(added == 2)\n        #expect(Set(group.contacts.map(\\.persistentModelID)) == [ada.persistentModelID, alan.persistentModelID])\n    }\n\n    @Test func skipsExistingMembersAndUnknownIDs() throws {\n        let group = try store.createGroup(named: \"Work\")\n        let ada = try store.createContact(in: group) // already a member\n        let alan = try store.createContact()\n        let adaID = try #require(ada.persistentModelID.storedString)\n        let alanID = try #require(alan.persistentModelID.storedString)\n\n        // Ada is already in the group; \"garbage\" resolves to no contact.\n        let added = try store.addContacts(withEncodedIDs: [adaID, alanID, \"garbage\"], to: group)\n        #expect(added == 1)\n        #expect(group.contacts.count == 2)\n    }\n\n    @Test func isANoOpForEmptyInput() throws {\n        let group = try store.createGroup(named: \"Work\")\n        #expect(try store.addContacts(withEncodedIDs: [], to: group) == 0)\n    }\n}\n"
}

ID 3368483359 — ContactManager/Views/SidebarView.swift:58
`.dropDestination` currently returns `true` for any dropped `String`, even when the payload isn’t a contact id (or is empty). This makes unrelated text drops appear “accepted” despite doing nothing, and it diverges from the list’s `.vcf` drop handler which returns `false` for irrelevant drops. Filter to valid encoded `PersistentIdentifier`s and return `false` when none are present before calling `addContacts`.

ID 3368483364 — ContactManager/Models/ContactStore.swift:123
`addContacts(withEncodedIDs:to:)` treats arbitrary strings (including empty string) as candidate ids and will fetch *all* contacts even when nothing can possibly resolve (e.g. an unrelated text drop). Since this method is the data-path for drag/drop, it should first validate/normalize the encoded ids (using `PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored:)`) and early-return when none decode; this avoids unnecessary fetches and removes the `?? ""` equality edge case.

> AGENT

The test failure reveals that decoded-`PersistentIdentifier` equality doesn't hold for persisted models (a SwiftData quirk) — so matching by `==` returns nothing, even though the canonical `storedString` strings match. So Copilot's "match by decoded identifier" would actually break it. I'll keep the spirit (validate via `decode`, early-return, drop the `?? ""`) but match by the canonical encoded string, which is reliable:

  "new_string": "        // Keep only well-formed encoded ids; unrelated text (an empty string, a\n        // stray drop) decodes to nothing and short-circuits the fetch. We match\n        // on the canonical encoded string rather than `PersistentIdentifier`\n        // equality, which doesn't hold for a decoded-vs-live persisted id.\n        let wanted = Set(ids.filter { PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: $0) != nil })\n        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return 0 }\n        let groupID = group.persistentModelID\n        let toAdd = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<Contact>()).filter { contact in\n            guard let encoded = contact.persistentModelID.storedString else { return false }\n            return wanted.contains(encoded)\n                && !contact.groups.contains { $0.persistentModelID == groupID }\n        }"

2	//  ContentView+Import.swift
3	//  ContactManager
4	//
5	//  Import handlers (system Contacts, vCard file picker, vCard URL drops)
6	//  factored out of `ContentView` so the main view stays focused on
7	//  composition and state. Each handler runs the parse off the main
8	//  actor and routes inserts through `ContactStore` so they participate
9	//  in the existing Undo group.
10	//
11	
12	import Foundation
13	import SwiftUI
14	
15	private enum CSVImportOutcome {
16	    case parsed([ParsedContact])
17	    case unrecognized
18	    case unreadable
19	}
20	
21	extension ContentView {
22	    // MARK: - System Contacts import
23	
24	    func importSystemContacts() {
25	        Task {
26	            // Permission prompt + fetch + mapping all run off the main actor;
27	            // only the final insert hops back here.
28	            let parsed: [ParsedContact]
29	            do {
30	                parsed = try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
31	                    try await ContactsBridge.fetchAllParsed()
32	                }.value
33	            } catch {
34	                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
35	                return
36	            }
37	            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {
38	                errorMessage = "No contacts were found in your system Contacts."
39	                return
40	            }
41	            do {
42	                try store.importContacts(parsed)
43	            } catch {
44	                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
45	            }
46	        }
47	    }
48	
49	    // MARK: - vCard import

51	    /// Imports one or more vCard files dropped onto the contact list.
52	    func importVCardURLs(_ urls: [URL]) {
53	        Task {
54	            let parsed: [ParsedContact] = await Task.detached {
55	                var all: [ParsedContact] = []
56	                for url in urls {
57	                    let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
58	                    defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }
59	                    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
60	                          let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
61	                    else { continue }
62	                    all.append(contentsOf: VCard.parse(text))
63	                }
64	                return all
65	            }.value
66	
67	            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {
68	                errorMessage = "No contacts were found in that file."
69	                return
70	            }
71	            do {
72	                try store.importContacts(parsed)
73	            } catch {
74	                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
75	            }
76	        }
77	    }

79	    // MARK: - CSV import
80	
81	    func handleCSVImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {
82	        switch result {
83	        case .failure(let error):
84	            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
85	        case .success(let url):
86	            Task {
87	                let outcome: CSVImportOutcome = await Task.detached {
88	                    let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
89	                    defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }
90	                    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else { return .unreadable }
91	                    // CSV exports are commonly UTF-8 but Excel still emits
92	                    // UTF-16 with a BOM; try both before giving up.
93	                    let text: String

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/Chunking.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  Chunking.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Splits a collection into fixed-size batches. Used to import contacts a\n//  chunk at a time (one save + progress tick per chunk) instead of building\n//  the whole set on the main actor in a single mega-undo step.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nextension Array {\n    /// Splits the array into consecutive sub-arrays of at most `size` elements.\n    /// A non-positive `size` returns the whole array as a single chunk (or no\n    /// chunks when empty), so callers can't accidentally spin forever.\n    func chunked(into size: Int) -> [[Element]] {\n        guard size > 0 else { return isEmpty ? [] : [self] }\n        return stride(from: 0, to: count, by: size).map {\n            Array(self[$0 ..< Swift.min($0 + size, count)])\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Views/ImportProgressView.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ImportProgressView.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  A small modal-style overlay shown while a vCard/CSV/system-Contacts import\n//  is parsing and inserting, so a large file no longer looks like a frozen UI.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n/// State for the import overlay. `total == nil` means the parse phase is still\n/// running (indeterminate); once inserting begins, `total` is the contact count\n/// and `done` climbs per saved chunk.\nstruct ImportProgress: Equatable {\n    var done = 0\n    var total: Int?\n}\n\nstruct ImportProgressView: View {\n    let progress: ImportProgress\n\n    var body: some View {\n        VStack(spacing: 12) {\n            if let total = progress.total {\n                ProgressView(value: Double(progress.done), total: Double(max(total, 1))) {\n                    Text(\"Importing Contacts\")\n                }\n                Text(\"\\(progress.done) of \\(total)\")\n                    .font(.caption)\n                    .monospacedDigit()\n                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)\n            } else {\n                ProgressView { Text(\"Preparing Import…\") }\n            }\n        }\n        .padding(24)\n        .frame(width: 260)\n        .background(.regularMaterial, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))\n        .shadow(radius: 20)\n        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)\n        .accessibilityLabel(accessibilityLabel)\n    }\n\n    private var accessibilityLabel: String {\n        guard let total = progress.total else { return \"Preparing import\" }\n        return \"Importing contacts, \\(progress.done) of \\(total)\"\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "old_string": "    func importSystemContacts() {\n        Task {\n            // Permission prompt + fetch + mapping all run off the main actor;\n            // only the final insert hops back here.\n            let parsed: [ParsedContact]\n            do {\n                parsed = try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {\n                    try await ContactsBridge.fetchAllParsed()\n                }.value\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                return\n            }\n            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {\n                errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in your system Contacts.\"\n                return\n            }\n            do {\n                try store.importContacts(parsed)\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n            }\n        }\n    }",
  "new_string": "    func importSystemContacts() {\n        Task {\n            importProgress = ImportProgress()\n            defer { importProgress = nil }\n            // Permission prompt + fetch + mapping all run off the main actor;\n            // only the final insert hops back here.\n            let parsed: [ParsedContact]\n            do {\n                parsed = try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {\n                    try await ContactsBridge.fetchAllParsed()\n                }.value\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                return\n            }\n            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {\n                errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in your system Contacts.\"\n                return\n            }\n            await insert(parsed)\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Chunked insert + progress\n\n    /// Inserts parsed contacts a chunk at a time — one save (and undo step) per\n    /// chunk instead of one giant transaction — updating `importProgress` and\n    /// yielding between chunks so the overlay animates rather than freezing.\n    func insert(_ parsed: [ParsedContact]) async {\n        importProgress = ImportProgress(done: 0, total: parsed.count)\n        do {\n            for chunk in parsed.chunked(into: 500) {\n                try store.importContacts(chunk)\n                importProgress?.done += chunk.count\n                await Task.yield()\n            }\n        } catch {\n            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n        }\n    }"
}

Standalone — it reads only the contact, so\n//  it renders the same off-screen as it would on-screen.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct PrintableContactView: View {\n    let contact: Contact\n\n    private let width: CGFloat = 480\n\n    var body: some View {\n        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {\n            header\n            Divider()\n            fields(contact.emails, title: \"Email\")\n            fields(contact.phones, title: \"Phone\")\n            address\n            birthday\n            notes\n        }\n        .padding(32)\n        .frame(width: width, alignment: .leading)\n        .background(.white)\n        .foregroundStyle(.black)\n    }\n\n    private var header: some View {\n        HStack(spacing: 16) {\n            AvatarView(contact: contact, size: 64)\n            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {\n                Text(contact.fullName)\n                    .font(.title.weight(.semibold))\n                let role = [contact.jobTitle, contact.company]\n                    .filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n                    .joined(separator: \" · \")\n                if !role.isEmpty {\n                    Text(role).font(.headline).foregroundStyle(.secondary)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    @ViewBuilder\n    private func fields(_ fields: [ContactField], title: String) -> some View {\n        let nonEmpty = fields.filter { !$0.value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty }\n        if !nonEmpty.isEmpty {\n            section(title) {\n                ForEach(nonEmpty) { field in\n                    labeledRow(field.label.title, field.value)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    @ViewBuilder\n    private var address: some View {\n        let lines = [\n            contact.street,\n            [contact.city, contact.state, contact.postalCode]\n                .filter { !$0.isEmpty }.joined(separator: \" \"),\n            contact.country,\n        ].filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n        if !lines.isEmpty {\n            section(\"Address\") {\n                ForEach(lines, id: \\.self) { Text($0) }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    @ViewBuilder\n    private var birthday: some View {\n        if let date = contact.birthday {\n            section(\"Birthday\") {\n                Text(formattedBirthday(date))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    @ViewBuilder\n    private var notes: some View {\n        if !contact.notes.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty {\n            section(\"Notes\") {\n                Text(contact.notes)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func section(_ title: String, @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View) -> some View {\n        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {\n            Text(title.uppercased())\n                .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))\n                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)\n            content()\n                .font(.body)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func labeledRow(_ label: String, _ value: String) -> some View {\n        HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline) {\n            Text(label).foregroundStyle(.secondary).frame(width: 64, alignment: .leading)\n            Text(value)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func formattedBirthday(_ date: Date) -> String {\n        let fields = Birthday.fields(of: date)\n        let months = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian).monthSymbols\n        let month = (1 ... 12).contains(fields.month) ? months[fields.month - 1] : \"\"\n        if let year = fields.year {\n            return \"\\(month) \\(fields.day), \\(year)\"\n        }\n        return \"\\(month) \\(fields.day)\"\n    }\n}\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/ContactPDF.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactPDF.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Renders a contact's printable card (PrintableContactView) to PDF data via\n//  ImageRenderer, and prints it through PDFKit. Kept out of the view so the\n//  PDF generation can be unit-tested.\n//\n\nimport PDFKit\nimport SwiftUI\n\n@MainActor\nenum ContactPDF {\n    /// PDF bytes for a single contact's card, or `nil` if rendering fails.\n    /// The page is sized to the rendered card.\n    static func data(for contact: Contact) -> Data? {\n        let renderer = ImageRenderer(content: PrintableContactView(contact: contact))\n        let pdfData = NSMutableData()\n        var result: Data?\n        // ImageRenderer.render runs its closure synchronously; we build a\n        // one-page PDF context the size of the rendered card.\n        renderer.render { size, renderInContext in\n            var mediaBox = CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)\n            guard let consumer = CGDataConsumer(data: pdfData as CFMutableData),\n                  let context = CGContext(consumer: consumer, mediaBox: &mediaBox, nil)\n            else { return }\n            context.beginPDFPage(nil)\n            renderInContext(context)\n            context.endPDFPage()\n            context.closePDF()\n            result = pdfData as Data\n        }\n        return result\n    }\n\n    /// A file-system-safe filename stem (no extension) for the contact's PDF.\n    static func filename(for contact: Contact) -> String {\n        VCardTransfer.suggestedFilename(for: contact.fullName)\n    }\n\n    /// Presents the system print sheet for the contact's card.\n    static func print(_ contact: Contact) -> Bool {\n        guard let data = data(for: contact), let document = PDFDocument(data: data) else {\n            return false\n        }\n        let info = NSPrintInfo.shared\n        guard let operation = document.printOperation(\n            for: info, scalingMode: .pageScaleToFit, autoRotate: false\n        ) else { return false }\n        operation.run()\n        return true\n    }\n}\n"
}

Data()\n    }\n\n    func fileWrapper(configuration _: WriteConfiguration) throws -> FileWrapper {\n        FileWrapper(regularFileWithContents: data)\n    }\n}\n"
}

String\n                selectContact(byEncodedID: id)\n            }\n    }\n\n    /// The sheets, importers, exporters, and the error alert.\n    func handlingFileDialogs(_ content: some View) -> some View {\n        content\n            .sheet(isPresented: $showingDuplicates) {\n                DuplicatesView()\n            }\n            .fileImporter(isPresented: $isImportingVCard, allowedContentTypes: [.vCard]) { result in\n                handleImport(result)\n            }\n            .fileImporter(isPresented: $isImportingCSV, allowedContentTypes: [.commaSeparatedText]) { result in\n                handleCSVImport(result)\n            }\n            .fileExporter(\n                isPresented: $isExportingVCard,\n                document: exportDocument,\n                contentType: .vCard,\n                defaultFilename: \"Contacts\"\n            ) { result in\n                if case .failure(let error) = result {\n                    errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                }\n            }\n            .fileExporter(\n                isPresented: $isExportingPDF,\n                document: pdfDocument,\n                contentType: .pdf,\n                defaultFilename: pdfFilename\n            ) { result in\n                if case .failure(let error) = result {\n                    errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                }\n            }\n            .alert(\n                \"Something Went Wrong\",\n                isPresented: Binding(get: { errorMessage != nil }, set: { if !$0 { errorMessage = nil } }),\n                presenting: errorMessage\n            ) { _ in\n                Button(\"OK\", role: .cancel) {}\n            } message: { message in\n                Text(message)\n            }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: -   "new_string": "    /// Presents the system print panel for the contact's card — as a\n    /// window-attached sheet when there's a key window, otherwise app-modal.\n    static func print(_ contact: Contact) -> Bool {\n        guard let data = data(for: contact), let document = PDFDocument(data: data) else {\n            return false\n        }\n        guard let operation = document.printOperation(\n            for: NSPrintInfo.shared, scalingMode: .pageScaleToFit, autoRotate: false\n        ) else { return false }\n        if let window = NSApp.keyWindow {\n            operation.runModal(for: window, delegate: nil, didRun: nil, contextInfo: nil)\n        } else {\n            operation.run()\n        }\n        return true\n    }"

{

  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Views/ContactWindowView.swift",
  "old_string": "    let encodedID: String?\n\n    @Query(sort: [SortDescriptor(\\Contact.lastName), SortDescriptor(\\Contact.firstName)])\n    private var contacts: [Contact]\n\n    private var contact: Contact? {\n        guard let encodedID,\n              let id = PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: encodedID)\n        else { return nil }\n        return contacts.first { $0.persistentModelID == id }\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let contact {\n                ContactDetailView(contact: contact)\n                    .navigationTitle(contact.fullName)\n            } else {\n                ContentUnavailableView(\n                    \"Contact Not Found\",\n                    systemImage: \"person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark\",\n                    description: Text(\n                        \"This window's contact may have been deleted. \" +\n                            \"Close the window or open another contact from the main window.\"\n                    )\n                )\n            }\n        }\n        .frame(minWidth: 460, minHeight: 520)\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "    let encodedID: String?\n\n    @Query(sort: [SortDescriptor(\\Contact.lastName), SortDescriptor(\\Contact.firstName)])\n    private var contacts: [Contact]\n\n    @Environment(\\.dismiss) private var dismiss\n    /// Whether this window ever showed its contact. Lets us tell \"deleted\n    /// while open\" (auto-close) from \"never resolved\" — a stale id at launch /\n    /// window restoration — where we keep the explanatory unavailable view.\n    @State private var hadContact = false\n\n    private var contact: Contact? {\n        guard let encodedID,\n              let id = PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: encodedID)\n        else { return nil }\n        return contacts.first { $0.persistentModelID == id }\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let contact {\n                ContactDetailView(contact: contact)\n                    .navigationTitle(contact.fullName)\n                    .onAppear { hadContact = true }\n            } else {\n                ContentUnavailableView(\n                    \"Contact Not Found\",\n                    systemImage: \"person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark\",\n                    description: Text(\n                        \"This window's contact may have been deleted. \" +\n                            \"Close the window or open another contact from the main window.\"\n                    )\n                )\n                // If we'd previously shown the contact, it was just deleted —\n                // close the now-orphaned window instead of stranding it.\n                .onAppear { if hadContact { dismiss() } }\n            }\n        }\n        .frame(minWidth: 460, minHeight: 520)\n    }\n}"

2	//  ContactWindowView.swift
3	//  ContactManager
4	//
5	//  The single-contact detached window — opened via the row context menu
6	//  ("Open in New Window"). The window receives the contact's encoded
7	//  `PersistentIdentifier` (same string scheme used by App Intents and
8	//  the default-group preference) and resolves it to a live `Contact`
9	//  out of the shared model container.
10	//
11	//  Edits flow through the same `ContactStore` the main window uses, so
12	//  changes appear in both places and join the main app's undo stack.
13	//
14	
15	import SwiftData
16	import SwiftUI
17	
18	struct ContactWindowView: View {
19	    /// JSON-encoded `PersistentIdentifier`. Optional only because
20	    /// `WindowGroup`'s binding hands us `String?` — an empty value is
21	    /// treated the same as a missing contact below.
22	    let encodedID: String?
23	
24	    @Query(sort: [SortDescriptor(\Contact.lastName), SortDescriptor(\Contact.firstName)])
25	    private var contacts: [Contact]
26	
27	    private var contact: Contact? {
28	        guard let encodedID,
29	              let id = PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: encodedID)
30	        else { return nil }
31	        return contacts.first { $0.persistentModelID == id }
32	    }
33	
34	    var body: some View {
35	        Group {
36	            if let contact {
37	                ContactDetailView(contact: contact)
38	                    .navigationTitle(contact.fullName)
39	            } else {

41	                    "Contact Not Found",
42	                    systemImage: "person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark",
43	                    description: Text(
44	                        "This window's contact may have been deleted. " +
45	                            "Close the window or open another contact from the main window."
46	                    )
47	                )
48	            }
49	        }
50	        .frame(minWidth: 460, minHeight: 520)
51	    }
52	}

  "new_string": "    @Query(sort: [SortDescriptor(\\Contact.lastName), SortDescriptor(\\Contact.firstName)])\n    private var contacts: [Contact]\n\n    @Environment(\\.dismiss) private var dismiss\n    /// Whether this window ever showed its contact. Lets us tell \"deleted\n    /// while open\" (auto-close) from \"never resolved\" — a stale id at launch /\n    /// window restoration — where we keep the explanatory unavailable view.\n    @State private var hadContact = false\n\n    private var contact: Contact? {\n        guard let encodedID,\n              let id = PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: encodedID)\n        else { return nil }\n        return contacts.first { $0.persistentModelID == id }\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let contact {\n                ContactDetailView(contact: contact)\n                    .navigationTitle(contact.fullName)\n                    .onAppear { hadContact = true }\n            } else {\n                ContentUnavailableView(\n                    \"Contact Not Found\",\n                    systemImage: \"person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark\",\n                    description: Text(\n                        \"This window's contact may have been deleted. \" +\n                            \"Close the window or open another contact from the main window.\"\n                    )\n                )\n                // If we'd previously shown the contact, it was just deleted —\n                // close the now-orphaned window instead of stranding it.\n                .onAppear { if hadContact { dismiss() } }\n            }\n        }\n        .frame(minWidth: 460, minHeight: 520)\n    }\n}"

//
//  OpenContactIntent.swift
//  ContactManager
//
//  Shortcut/Siri action: brings ContactManager forward and selects the
//  chosen contact. The actual navigation is handled by `ContentView`
//  observing `Notification.Name.openContactRequested`.
//

import AppIntents
import Foundation

struct OpenContactIntent: AppIntent {
    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "Open Contact"
    static let description = IntentDescription(
        "Opens ContactManager and selects the chosen contact."
    )
    /// Tells the system to launch the app for us before `perform()` runs.
    static let openAppWhenRun = true

    @Parameter(title: "Contact") var target: ContactEntity

    @MainActor
    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {
        NotificationCenter.default.post(
            name: .openContactRequested,
            object: nil,
            userInfo: ["id": target.id]
        )
        return .result()
    }
}

    /// and the main window renders. Catches the "WindowGroup body
    /// silently rendered EmptyView" failure mode the unit tests can't
    /// see — the rest of the journey (seeded data, list interaction,
    /// edits) is covered by the unit-test layer.
    func test_appLaunchesWithMainWindow() {
        let app = bootSeededApp()
        XCTAssertTrue(app.windows.firstMatch.exists)
        // The search field anchors the contact-list toolbar; if it's
        // present the main list rendered, not the StoreErrorView fallback.
        XCTAssertTrue(
            app.searchFields.firstMatch.waitForExistence(timeout: 3),
            "Contact-list search field should render"
        )
    }

    /// Verifies the File menu wires the Import / Export commands the
    /// unit tests can't probe directly.
    func test_fileMenuExposesImportAndExportCommands() {
        let app = bootSeededApp()
        app.menuBars.menuBarItems["File"].click()
        XCTAssertTrue(app.menuItems["New Contact"].exists)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.menuItems["Import from Contacts…"].exists)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.menuItems["Import vCard…"].exists)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.menuItems["Import CSV…"].exists)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.menuItems["Export vCard…"].exists)
    }

    /// Verifies Edit ▸ Find Duplicates… opens the sheet. Sheet content
    /// is covered by `DuplicateFinder` + `ContactStore.merge` unit tests.
    func test_findDuplicatesShortcutOpensTheSheet() {
        let app = bootSeededApp()
        app.typeKey("d", modifierFlags: [.command, .shift])
        XCTAssertTrue(
            app.buttons["Done"].waitForExistence(timeout: 3),
            "Duplicates sheet's Done button should appear after ⌘⇧D"
        )
    }

    // MARK: - Helpers

    /// Launches a fresh app instance with the seeded UI-test container.
    /// Returns the `XCUIApplication` so each test can scope its
    /// assertions to a known-good handle.
    private func bootSeededApp() -> XCUIApplication {
        app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launchEnvironment["CONTACTMANAGER_UI_TEST_MODE"] = "1"
        app.launchArguments = ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES"]
        app.launch()
        XCTAssertTrue(
            app.windows.firstMatch.waitForExistence(timeout: 10),
            "Main window didn't appear within 10s"
        )
        return app
    }
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/DefaultGroupPreference.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  DefaultGroupPreference.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Resolves the \"new contacts join this group\" preference (an encoded\n//  `PersistentIdentifier` in @AppStorage) against the live groups. Pulled out\n//  of the views so the matching — and the stale/renamed/deleted handling — is\n//  unit-tested.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nenum DefaultGroupPreference {\n    /// The group the stored preference points at, or `nil` when it's empty,\n    /// undecodable, or its target was deleted.\n    ///\n    /// Matches on the *canonical encoded id* rather than `PersistentIdentifier`\n    /// equality: a value decoded from a string doesn't compare equal to the\n    /// live persisted id, so `==` would never match a saved group. Decoding\n    /// first also lets an older, non-canonically-encoded stored value still\n    /// resolve (decode is key-order independent; re-encoding canonicalizes it).\n    static func group(stored: String, in groups: [ContactGroup]) -> ContactGroup? {\n        guard let canonical = PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: stored)?.storedString else {\n            return nil\n        }\n        return groups.first { $0.persistentModelID.storedString == canonical }\n    }\n\n    /// The value the preference should hold: the matched group's canonical id,\n    /// or `\"\"` when it points at nothing — so a blank, stale, deleted, or\n    /// old-format value self-heals to a consistent state.\n    static func normalized(stored: String, in groups: [ContactGroup]) -> String {\n        group(stored: stored, in: groups)?.persistentModelID.storedString ?? \"\"\n    }\n}\n"
}

A value written by\n        // an older build used a non-deterministic key order, so its string\n        // wouldn't match the freshly-encoded picker tags; normalizing here\n        // keeps the selection highlighted without a separate migration.\n        if let canonical = id.storedString, canonical != defaultGroupID {\n            defaultGroupID = canonical\n        }\n    }\n}",

}

=== README ===
# Contact Manager

**ContactManager** is a native macOS contact manager built with **SwiftUI** and **SwiftData**, targeting the modern macOS Tahoe (macOS 26) look and feel. It is **100% self-contained** with zero third-party dependencies.

The app was originally an Objective-C / AppKit / Core Data demo and was rebuilt, in focused increments, into a polished native Tahoe application.

---

## Architecture

- **Platform**: macOS 26.0+ (Tahoe)
- **UI**: SwiftUI — a three-column `NavigationSplitView` (sidebar / contact list / detail) that automatically adopts the Liquid Glass appearance when built against the macOS 26 SDK.
- **Persistence**: SwiftData (`@Model`, `ModelContainer`, `@Query`), replacing the legacy Core Data stack.
- **Language**: Swift
- **Testing**: Swift Testing, backed by an in-memory `ModelContainer`.

### Source layout

```
ContactManager/
├── App/      ContactManagerApp.swift   – @main entry point, model container, menu commands
├── Models/   Contact.swift             – the @Model contact entity + derived values
│             ContactField.swift        – labeled, repeatable email/phone child entity
│             ContactGroup.swift        – user group/tag (many-to-many with Contact)
│             ContactQuery.swift        – pure, testable filter/sort/section helpers
│             SampleData.swift          – first-launch seed data
├── Support/  ImageProcessing.swift     – downscales picked images into avatar JPEGs
│             VCard.swift               – pure vCard 3.0 reader/writer
│             VCardDocument.swift       – FileDocument for the export dialog
└── Views/    ContentView.swift         – NavigationSplitView shell, group + import/export logic
              SidebarView.swift         – groups sidebar with create/rename/delete
              ContactListView.swift     – searchable, sectioned contact list + toolbar
              ContactDetailView.swift   – editable detail form + photo well + group toggles
              AvatarView.swift          – photo or initials avatar with a per-contact tint
```

---

## Features

- Three-column native layout with a Liquid Glass toolbar and a toggleable trailing inspector pane.
- Create, edit (inline, autosaving), and delete contacts.
- Multiple labeled emails and phone numbers per contact (add/remove inline).
- Company, job title, postal address, birthday, and free-form notes.
- Live search across name, company, title, notes, and field values.
- Alphabetical sections with a first-name / last-name sort toggle.
- Contact photos (downscaled on import) with an initials avatar fallback.
- User-defined groups (sidebar create/rename/delete) with per-contact membership.
- vCard 3.0 import and export (File ▸ Import/Export vCard…), including embedded **PHOTO** round-tripping.
- Duplicate detection & merge (Edit ▸ Find Duplicates…) — review and combine contacts that share an email, phone, or name.
- iCloud sync (when the iCloud capability is enabled in Xcode) with a graceful local-only fallback when it isn't.
- Liquid Glass styling, glass-prominent actions, and smooth list/selection animations.

### Roadmap

Shipped as small, single-purpose PRs:

1. ✅ **Foundation** — SwiftUI + SwiftData rewrite, CRUD, project modernized to macOS 26.
2. ✅ **Richer fields** — multiple emails/phones, company/title, address, birthday, notes.
3. ✅ **Search & sections** — live search and alphabetical sectioning.
4. ✅ **Contact photos** — photo import with initials fallback.
5. ✅ **Groups & vCard** — user groups/tags and `.vcf` import/export.
6. ✅ **Tahoe polish** — Liquid Glass refinements, animations, and richer empty states.

---

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

Xcode 26 or later (macOS 26 SDK). No dependency managers required.

### Building & Running

Open `ContactManager.xcodeproj` in Xcode, select the **ContactManager** scheme, and press `Cmd + R`.

### Running the Test Suite

```shell
xcodebuild -project ContactManager.xcodeproj -scheme ContactManager -destination 'platform=macOS' test
```
```

  "content": "# Contact Manager\n\n**ContactManager** is a native macOS contact manager built with **SwiftUI** and **SwiftData**, targeting the modern macOS Tahoe (macOS 26) look and feel. It has **zero third-party runtime dependencies**.\n\nThe app was originally an Objective-C / AppKit / Core Data demo and was rebuilt, in focused increments, into a polished native Tahoe application.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n- **Platform**: macOS 26.0+ (Tahoe)\n- **UI**: SwiftUI — a three-column `NavigationSplitView` (groups sidebar / contact list / detail) that automatically adopts the Liquid Glass appearance when built against the macOS 26 SDK.\n- **Persistence**: SwiftData (`@Model`, `ModelContainer`, `@Query`), replacing the legacy Core Data stack. The container is **CloudKit-ready** (`cloudKitDatabase: .automatic`) and falls back to a local-only store when no iCloud capability is present.\n- **System integration**: App Intents (Shortcuts / Siri), Core Spotlight indexing, the macOS Contacts framework, and drag-and-drop.\n- **Language**: Swift (language mode 5; full Swift 6 concurrency is a future migration).\n- **Testing**: Swift Testing (unit) backed by an in-memory `ModelContainer`, plus a small XCUITest smoke suite.\n\n### Source layout\n\n```\nContactManager/\n├── App/      ContactManagerApp.swift     – @main entry, ModelContainer, menu commands, scenes\n├── Models/   Contact.swift               – the @Model contact entity + derived values\n│             ContactField.swift          – labeled, repeatable email/phone child entity\n│             ContactGroup.swift          – user group/tag (many-to-many with Contact)\n│             ContactStore.swift          – data layer: every mutation, saved + undoable\n│             ContactQuery.swift          – pure filter/sort/section helpers\n│             DuplicateFinder.swift       – groups likely-duplicate contacts\n│             DefaultGroupPreference.swift – resolves the \"new contacts join\" preference\n│             SampleData.swift            – first-launch seed data\n├── Support/  VCard.swift / VCardDocument.swift / VCardTransfer.swift – vCard 3.0 read/write, export, drag\n│             CSV.swift                   – Google/Outlook/Apple CSV reader\n│             ContactsBridge.swift        – import from the macOS Contacts app\n│             ImageProcessing.swift       – downscales picked images into avatar JPEGs\n│             Birthday.swift              – UTC-anchored date-only birthday handling\n│             ContactLink.swift           – mailto:/tel: URL construction\n│             ContactPDF.swift / PDFExportDocument.swift – contact-card PDF render + export\n│             Chunking.swift              – batches large imports\n│             SpotlightIndexer.swift      – incremental Core Spotlight indexing\n│             PersistentIdentifierEncoding.swift – stable encoded model ids\n├── Intents/  ContactEntity / ContactEntityQuery – App Intents identity + Spotlight attributes\n│             FindContactIntent / OpenContactIntent – Shortcuts/Siri actions\n│             EntityModelContainer.swift  – process-wide container handle for intents\n└── Views/    ContentView (+Import)       – split-view shell, selection, import/export, progress\n              SidebarView                 – groups sidebar (create/rename/delete, drop target)\n              ContactListView             – searchable, sectioned list + toolbar + drag\n              ContactDetailView (+Photo, +Birthday) – editable detail, photo well, share, actions\n              ContactWindowView           – single-contact detached window\n              PrintableContactView        – print/PDF card layout\n              SettingsView · DuplicatesView · ImportProgressView · AvatarView · LayoutMetrics\n```\n\n---\n\n## Features\n\n- Three-column native layout with a Liquid Glass toolbar and smooth list/selection animations.\n- Create, edit (inline, autosaving), and delete contacts, with full **Undo/Redo** (⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z).\n- Multiple labeled emails and phone numbers, company, job title, postal address, birthday (year optional), and notes.\n- Click-to-mail / click-to-call (`mailto:` / `tel:`) on the contact's primary email and phone.\n- Live, debounced search across name, company, title, notes, and field values, with alphabetical sections and a first-name / last-name sort toggle. **⌘F** focuses the search field.\n- Contact photos (downscaled on import, streamed via ImageIO) with an initials avatar fallback.\n- User-defined groups (sidebar create/rename/delete); drag contacts onto a group to add them.\n- Duplicate detection & merge (Edit ▸ Find Duplicates…).\n- **Import**: vCard `.vcf`, CSV (Google / Outlook / Apple exports), and the macOS **Contacts** app — chunked with a progress overlay. **Export / share**: vCard via File ▸ Export or the detail Share button.\n- **Print** a contact card and **Export as PDF** (⌘P / ⇧⌘P).\n- **Drag and drop**: drag a contact to Finder as a `.vcf`, drop a `.vcf` onto the list to import, drop an image onto the avatar.\n- **Open in New Window** for a single contact (closes itself if that contact is deleted).\n- **Shortcuts & Siri** via App Intents (Find / Open Contact) and **Spotlight** indexing with tap-to-open.\n- **iCloud sync** when the capability is enabled in Xcode, with a graceful local-only fallback.\n- Runs under the **App Sandbox** with hardened runtime.\n\n---\n\n## Development\n\nA `Makefile` wraps the common tasks (install tooling once with `make bootstrap`, which runs `brew bundle`):\n\n| Task | Command |\n| --- | --- |\n| Build | `make build` |\n| Test | `make test` |\n| Lint | `make lint` (autofix: `make lint-fix`) |\n| Format | `make format` (check only: `make format-check`) |\n| Pre-PR gate | `make check` (format-check + lint + test) |\n\nTests use **Swift Testing** (`import Testing`, `@Test`, `#expect`/`#require`). Linting and formatting are **SwiftLint** + **SwiftFormat**; CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `swiftformat --lint` and `swiftlint --strict` on every PR. Contributor and agent conventions live in `CLAUDE.md`.\n\n### Building & Running\n\nOpen `ContactManager.xcodeproj` in Xcode (26 or later, macOS 26 SDK), select the **ContactManager** scheme, and press `Cmd + R` — or run `make build`.\n\n### Running the Tests\n\n```shell\nmake test            # unit + UI tests via xcodebuild\n```\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/ContactActivity.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactActivity.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  The `NSUserActivity` for \"viewing a contact\" — advertised for Handoff so\n//  the contact open on one device can be continued on another, and consumed\n//  on the receiving side. The activity type is also declared in the app's\n//  Info.plist (INFOPLIST_KEY_NSUserActivityTypes) so the system advertises it.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum ContactActivity {\n    /// Handoff activity type for the currently open contact.\n    static let viewContactType = \"com.scottdensmore.ContactManager.viewContact\"\n    /// `userInfo` key holding the contact's encoded `PersistentIdentifier`.\n    static let idKey = \"id\"\n\n    /// Populates an activity (e.g. the one SwiftUI's `.userActivity` hands us)\n    /// to advertise the given contact for Handoff. Kept separate from the view\n    /// so the payload is unit-tested.\n    static func configure(_ activity: NSUserActivity, contactID: String, displayName: String) {\n        activity.title = displayName\n        activity.userInfo = [idKey: contactID]\n        activity.targetContentIdentifier = contactID\n        activity.isEligibleForHandoff = true\n        // Spotlight indexing is handled separately by `SpotlightIndexer`.\n        activity.isEligibleForSearch = false\n    }\n\n    /// The encoded contact id carried by a continued activity, if any.\n    static func contactID(from activity: NSUserActivity) -> String? {\n        activity.userInfo?[idKey] as? String\n    }\n}\n"
}

ID 3368563180 — ContactManager/Views/ContentView.swift:303
`.userActivity` is marked active whenever `selectedContact != nil`, but if the selected contact's `persistentModelID.storedString` is `nil` (possible when encoding fails), the closure won't configure the activity. That can leave the system with an active activity lacking a valid identifier (or potentially stale payload), which can cause Handoff continuation to target the wrong contact or fail unpredictably. Consider only activating the activity when you have an encoded id.
---
ID 3368563188 — ContactManager/Support/ContactActivity.swift:8
The header comment references `INFOPLIST_KEY_NSUserActivityTypes`, but this PR actually declares the activity type via the `NSUserActivityTypes` key in `ContactManager/Info.plist` (because `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` doesn't support this array). Updating the comment would prevent future confusion/misconfiguration.
---
ID 3368563191 — ContactManager/Support/ContactActivity.swift:17
`NSUserActivity.userInfo` keys are shared dictionary keys and can collide with other producers/consumers (system keys or future app activities). Using a reverse-DNS namespaced key is safer and makes the payload more self-describing.
---
```

Nothing about CloudKit is committed to the project, so a download is never\nblocked by a provisioning profile you don't own.\n\nTo turn on sync for your own build:\n\n1. In Xcode, select the **ContactManager** target ▸ **Signing & Capabilities**.\n2. Set your **Team** (keep *Automatically manage signing*).\n3. Click **+ Capability** ▸ **Background Modes** and enable **Remote\n   notifications** so the store receives sync pushes.\n5. Make sure the Mac is signed in to iCloud, then build and run. The store now\n   syncs; on an empty CloudKit account your existing local contacts upload, and\n   other devices using the same container pull them down.\n\n> These steps modify the target's entitlements and signing settings. > AGENT

CloudKit shipped — and that was the **last item in the entire audit**. 🎉

## CloudKit — opt-in, non-blocking (PR #57, merged)

Exactly what you asked for: available, documented, never blocking a download.

- **At launch**, the app reads its *own* entitlements (`SecTask`) for a configured iCloud container:
  - **Configured** → `cloudKitDatabase: .automatic` → syncs across your devices, no sample seeding.
  - **Not configured** (a plain clone) → `.none` → local store, **seeded with sample contacts** so it's usable immediately.
- **Nothing CloudKit is committed** — no entitlement/container/team in the repo — so a clone never fails on a provisioning profile it doesn't own. Enabling sync is a documented opt-in (README ▸ *iCloud sync*: add iCloud ▸ CloudKit + a container + Push Notifications; don't commit those changes).
- **Fixed a latent bug along the way:** `.automatic` succeeds-as-local *without throwing* when there's no entitlement, so the old catch-based fallback never seeded a fresh local clone — it opened empty. Now it seeds correctly.
- Confirmed the SwiftData schema is CloudKit-compatible (defaults on all non-optional attributes, `[]` to-many, cascade/nullify rules, no `.unique`).

Copilot caught two real things (a redundant retry path; macOS uses *Push Notifications*, not iOS Background Modes) — both fixed.

## The whole audit is now cleared 🏁

| Tier | Items | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | App Sandbox (#39), Search perf (#40), Spotlight incremental (#41), **CloudKit (#57)** | ✅ all done |
| **P1** | 10 items — mailto/tel, birthday, photo, ShareLink, ⌘F, focus, group-drop, import progress+chunking, Print/PDF (#42–#50) | ✅ all done |
| **P2** | window-close, test gaps, README, Handoff, localization (#52–#56) + year-less picker (#51) | ✅ all done |

**Across the run:** PRs #39–#57, test suite **94 → 146**, every PR through the Copilot review loop, `make check` green. The app is now a ship-ready native macOS 26 SwiftUI + SwiftData contact manager with no outstanding audit items.

Nice place to stop — unless you want to tackle something net-new (e.g. an iOS/iPad target sharing the schema, or wiring up an actual CloudKit container on your side to smoke-test sync).

> DEVELOPER

What do I need to do to ensure that CloudSync works for me

> AGENT

Here's everything you need to flip on real sync. The code is already wired — at launch it checks your binary's entitlements for an iCloud container and switches to `cloudKitDatabase: .automatic` automatically, so **you won't touch any code.** It's all Xcode/Apple-account setup.

## Prerequisite
- A **paid Apple Developer Program** membership. CloudKit/iCloud capabilities are *not* available to a free "Personal Team" — Xcode will refuse to add the iCloud container without a paid team.

## In Xcode (target ▸ Signing & Capabilities)
1. **Signing**: turn on *Automatically manage signing* and pick your **Team** (the repo ships with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` empty on purpose). Bundle id is already `com.scottdensmore.ContactManager` — that's yours.
2. **+ Capability ▸ iCloud** → check **CloudKit** → add a container. The default **`iCloud.com.scottdensmore.ContactManager`** is fine.
3. **+ Capability ▸ Push Notifications** (this is the macOS capability that lets CloudKit deliver change pushes — there's no "Background Modes" toggle on a Mac target).

That's the switch. Those steps add `com.apple.developer.icloud-container-identifiers` to the entitlements, which is exactly what the app's `hasCloudKitEntitlement()` looks for — next launch it's in CloudKit mode (and stops seeding sample data).

## On the Mac
4. **Sign in to iCloud** (System Settings ▸ your Apple ID), iCloud Drive enabled, same account on every device you want to sync.

## First run — avoid uploading the sample contacts ⚠️
If you've run the app locally before, your store already contains the seeded **Ada / Alan / Grace** samples, and they'll upload to your real iCloud on first CloudKit run. To start clean, delete the local store **before** that first run:
```shell
rm -rf ~/Library/Containers/com.scottdensmore.ContactManager/Data/Library/Application\ Support/default.store*
```
(In CloudKit mode the app skips seeding, so it'll start empty and stay that way.)

## Verify it's actually syncing
- **CloudKit Console** (developer.apple.com ▸ CloudKit ▸ your container ▸ *Records*, Development env): add a contact, refresh, see the record.
- Or a **second Mac**: same app build, same container, same iCloud account → contacts appear within a few seconds.

## When you ship a release build
SwiftData auto-creates the schema in the **Development** environment. Before distributing, open the **CloudKit Console ▸ Deploy Schema Changes** to promote it to **Production** — otherwise a release/TestFlight build sees an empty production schema.

## Two notes
- **Keep these changes local — don't commit them.** The team + iCloud container + Push entitlement are what would break a clone for anyone without your account; leaving them uncommitted is what keeps the repo download-and-run for everyone.
- If sync silently doesn't happen after all of the above, add **App Sandbox ▸ Outgoing Connections (`com.apple.security.network.client`)** to the entitlements. CloudKit is normally brokered by a system daemon and works without it, but it's the first thing to try. (That one *is* safe to commit — it's a plain sandbox key with no team/container dependency.)

---

Done — PR #58 merged, so the README now carries the full walkthrough. Here's the version tailored to **your** machine (the docs cover the general case; you have a head start):

## Walk-through for you

**You can skip the team/membership step** — `SharedSettings.xcconfig` already sets your team `27ZDER873F`, and your bundle id is `com.scottdensmore.ContactManager`. So:

1. **Open the project** and select the **ContactManager** target ▸ **Signing & Capabilities** tab.
2. **+ Capability** → **iCloud** → tick **CloudKit** → under Containers, **+** and accept the default **`iCloud.com.scottdensmore.ContactManager`**. (Xcode registers it with your team.)
3. **+ Capability** → **Push Notifications** (lets CloudKit push changes to your other Macs).
4. **Sign in to iCloud** on this Mac if you aren't (System Settings ▸ Apple ID), same account on any device you'll sync with.
5. **Start clean so your sample contacts don't upload** (only when you're ready — this wipes the local store):
   ```shell
   rm -rf ~/Library/Containers/com.scottdensmore.ContactManager/Data/Library/Application\ Support/default.store*
   ```
6. **Build & run.** The app reads its entitlements at launch, sees the container, and switches to `cloudKitDatabase: .automatic` — no code change. It won't seed samples in this mode.
7. **Verify**: developer.apple.com ▸ **CloudKit Console** ▸ your container ▸ *Records* (Development) — add a contact, refresh, see it. Or a second Mac on the same account.

When you eventually ship a release build, do **CloudKit Console ▸ Deploy Schema Changes** to promote the schema to Production.

⚠️ **One thing to remember:** step 2–3 edit the committed `ContactManager.entitlements`. If you commit that, anyone who clones without your iCloud container can't sign/build. Keep that change local (don't commit it) to preserve the non-blocking design — that's the whole point of the runtime detection.

---

**Current UI tests (3, deliberately smoke-only):**
1. App launches + search field renders
2. File menu exposes New / Import (Contacts, vCard, CSV) / Export vCard
3. ⌘⇧D opens the Duplicates sheet

**Gaps I see:**
- **Stale menu test** — it predates several features. The File menu now also has **Export as PDF…** and **Print…**, and there's an Edit ▸ **Find** (⌘F) — none are asserted.
- **No "data actually renders" check** — the launch test confirms the search field exists, not that a seeded contact row (Ada/Alan/Grace) appears. That's the highest-value smoke signal (it'd catch an empty list / broken `@Query`).
- **No interaction journey** (create → edit → delete) — the original audit flagged this.
- **No accessibility identifiers anywhere in the app** — so any deeper test has to match on visible label text, which is the fragile part of macOS XCUITest.

**Two caveats that shape the call:** UI tests **aren't run in CI** (CI is swiftformat/swiftlint only), and they **flake locally on app activation** when the foreground is busy. So these earn their keep mainly when run in Xcode, not as an automated gate.
